data.name: Faid

data.long_meaning: One who assists and aids, Derived from the Arabic root 'f-d-d', meaning 'to help, support or aid'. A name deeply rooted in Islamic values and teachings. The name Faid carries the meaning “Helper” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Parents who choose Faid usually hope their child will grow to embody helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_arabic.long_meaning: فايد هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه الشخص النافع والمفيد، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع بمعنى الفائدة والمنفعة. و يعتبر من الأسماء المحببة في الثقافة الإسلامية لما يحمله من معاني جميلة وصفات حميدة.

in_urdu.name: فائد
in_urdu.meaning: فائد نام کا مطلب ہے مفید، نافع، فائدہ دینے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: فائد ایک مسلم نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے مفید، نافع یا فائدہ دینے والا۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیاء میں مسلمانوں کے درمیان میں بہت مقبول ہے کیونکہ اس میں مفید ہونے کی معانی ہیں۔

in_hindi.name: फैद
in_hindi.meaning: फैद नाम का अर्थ है उपयोगी, लाभदायक, फायदेमंद
in_hindi.long_meaning: फैद एक मुस्लिम नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है। इसका अर्थ है उपयोगी, लाभदायक या फायदेमंद। यह नाम भारत में मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत लोकप्रिय है क्योंकि इसमें उपयोगी होने की विशेषताएं हैं।

historical_references.reference: The Islamic name 'Faid' is believed to have originated from the Arabic word 'fa'idah', which means 'benefit' or 'profit'. It was commonly used as a personal name in the Islamic world during the medieval period.
historical_references.context: The term 'fa'idah' was used to signify the idea of personal gain or wealth, and was a popular name for both men and women during this period. The name 'Faid' was particularly common among merchants and traders, who saw the name as a symbol of their successful business ventures.

historical_references.reference: Another historical reference for the Islamic name 'Faid' comes from the account of Ibn Battuta, a 14th-century Muslim traveler. He mentions a town in present-day Algeria called 'Faid', which was an important trading center during the Berber Empire.
historical_references.context: The town of Faid was renowned for its strategic location along major trade routes, and was a hub for the exchange of goods between the Mediterranean and the Sahara. Ibn Battuta describes the prosperity of the town and its people, who were primarily merchants and traders, further highlighting the significance of the name 'Faid' as a symbol of profit and success.
